title: OPP officer describes shooting gas theft suspect: 'Completely shocked'
subtitle: A Chatham-Kent OPP officer became emotional at times testifying in court Thursday about what led to a Brantford man being shot on Highway 401 in July 2021.
article: A Chatham-Kent OPP officer became emotional while testifying in court Thursday about what led to a Brantford man being shot on Highway 401 in July 2021.
His voice choked with emotion, Const. Sean O'Rourke said, "I was in shock. I was horrified" after realizing his Glock semi-automatic pistol fired, hitting Nicholas Edward Grieves, 24.
The bullet severed two main arteries and Grieves died in hospital.
O'Rourke, who pleaded not guilty to manslaughter, took the stand on the fourth day of the trial in Superior Court in Chatham.

The incident stemmed from a call on July 7, 2021, shortly after 4:30 a.m., about the theft of $40 worth of gas from the Dutton ONroute rest stop. Police dispatch relayed the suspect vehicle was a gold-coloured car with a loud muffler travelling west on Highway 401.

O'Rourke said his training and experience in locating contraband, such as illegal weapons and drugs, raised concerns this was more than a routine theft of gas, especially because it happened so early in the morning.

O'Rourke and OPP Sgt. Bradley Cooper responded to the gas theft call. O'Rourke, who was driving an unmarked Dodge Durango, and Cooper, who was driving a marked OPP SUV, positioned their vehicles out of sight at the Orford Road underpass on Highway 401.

The officers followed a 2003 Pontiac Sunfire with a loud muffler when it passed. Not having their emergency lights activated as first, the officers planned a tandem stop with one vehicle in front and another behind, which is designed to safely get a vehicle off the road.
O'Rourke said the officers activated their emergency lights as part of the tandem stop.

O'Rourke described how the Sunfire, driven by Grieves with his fiancée Angela Keats in the front passenger seat, and Jonathan Wauthier in the back seat, rammed into his cruiser when he tried to block the car from getting past him.
"I've never had anybody ram my police cruiser," O'Rourke said. "It was very violent, very intentional and completely unexpected."
The Sunfire spun into the sloped median on the highway, but the driver was trying to get out, despite being stuck in deep mud.
O'Rourke described seeing Grieves with a "crazed look in his eyes," when the headlights of his cruiser provided a brief glimpse inside the vehicle.
The officer also testified Grieves was focused on the centre console of the vehicle, which raised concerns he was trying to get at a weapon.
Concerned for his safety, O'Rourke said he drew is firearm.
When he approached the vehicle, O'Rourke said he yelled commands, including, "Police don't move" and "Let me see your hands" as loud as he could over the Sunfire's loud muffler.
Neither Grieves or Keats raised their hands, he said.
O'Rourke described tripping and due to the angle of the slope he was on, he fell forward and ended up partially in the vehicle with his gun near Keats's face.
Noting his gun was accessible to both front-seat passengers, O'Rourke said, "I just wanted to get out of there."
It was in his struggle to free himself from the vehicle that his gun went off, he said.
"I was completely shocked," O'Rourke said. "I didn't know why, I didn't know how (it happened)."
Testifying that he had his finger on the slide of the weapon, not on the trigger, the officer said, "I can't figure out what happened."
The officer also recalled Cook coming up as they both arrived at the driver's side door and asking what happened.
"I told him, 'I shot him,'" O'Rourke said.
The officer said he hoped the shot was a "through and through" with the bullet passing through a limb.
But, when he saw Grieves was having laboured breathing, "I knew the round had entered his chest."
The two officers performed CPR until paramedics and firefighters arrived.
During this time, O'Rourke said Keats was over them, shouting, "You didn't have to shoot him.
"Why did you shoot him? He wasn't resisting."
O'Rourke returns to the stand Friday to be cross-examined by the Crown.
